events.title: Darwin and Wallace's Theories Presented in London
events.description: At the Linnean Society of London, papers by Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace were read together. Both set out the idea that species evolve through natural selection.
events.significance: This was the first public presentation of the theory of evolution by natural selection. It prepared the way for Darwin's 'On the Origin of Species' the following year.

events.title: Canada Becomes a Confederation
events.description: The British North America Act took effect. It united the colonies of Canada, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick as the Dominion of Canada. The anniversary was long celebrated as Dominion Day.
events.significance: This was the founding of modern Canada. The day is now marked every year as Canada Day, the national holiday.

events.title: The Battle of the Somme Begins
events.description: British and French forces launched a major offensive along the Somme River in France at 7:30 in the morning. The first day brought catastrophic casualties for the British Army, which suffered the heaviest losses in its history.
events.significance: The battle lasted until November and became a symbol of the immense human cost of trench warfare in the First World War.

events.title: Hong Kong Returns to Chinese Sovereignty
events.description: After 156 years of British rule, Hong Kong was handed over to China in a ceremony that ended its time as a British colony. It became a Special Administrative Region of China.
events.significance: The handover marked the end of a major chapter of the British Empire in Asia. It also began the 'one country, two systems' arrangement that continues to shape Hong Kong's status.
